turns.t: Mrs Iyer? Your booking says six-week postnatal check, so let us see how you and the baby are doing.
Yes, doctor. Baby is sleeping at my mother-in-law's place today. We are both fine, only I am a little tired.
A little tired. Tired how? All day long, or at a certain time?
By the evening mostly. In the morning I manage okay.
That is very common with a six-week-old. How many hours are you sleeping in total?
Maybe four, but broken. That is normal only, everyone says so.
Yes, quite normal. And how is your mood? Any low mood, crying spells, anything like that?
No, no. I am happy only. Just tired.
Good to hear. Are you feeding the baby yourself?
Yes, breastfeeding. Every three hours or so. She is feeding well, thank God.
Fine. Does any illness run in your family, say diabetes or thyroid problems? It matters for your check-ups later.
Just my mother. She has diabetes, for many years now.
Noted. Now I will check your pressure, pulse, temperature and weight. Please stand on the scale first.
Okay, doctor. I have been scared to check my weight since the delivery.
Weight is 64 kilograms. Blood pressure 112 over 70, pulse 76, temperature 36.6 degrees. All in order.
Sixty-four. That is less than I expected, actually.
Good. Now lie down, I will press gently on your tummy and check the womb.
Okay, go ahead.
The womb has gone back to its normal size, and it feels firm. The healing is as expected.
That is good to hear.
So overall, this looks like normal postnatal recovery. There is nothing for me to treat today.
Doctor, my husband is asking about family planning. What are the options?
Basically four. One, condoms, which you can start right away. Two, an implant in the upper arm. Three, a coil, copper or hormonal. Four, natural cycles, but that is least reliable.
Which one is better while breastfeeding?
Condoms, the implant and the copper coil are all fine. Some hormonal methods need more care, so we choose together.
Let me discuss at home first. For now we will manage with condoms.
Perfectly reasonable. Take your time deciding, there is no hurry on this.
Can I start exercise again? I used to do yoga before pregnancy.
Start with walking, thirty minutes a day. Add pelvic floor exercises, a few times daily. Slowly build up to yoga over the next month.
And lifting heavy things? The baby seat is very heavy.
Lift the baby, yes, but avoid very heavy loads for another few weeks. Let your husband carry the seat.
He will be happy to hear that. My mother-in-law is also staying with us for two months.
That is a big help, then. Do let her take the night feeds sometimes, if you are expressing.
Yes, both are very supportive. I am joining work after three months only.
That is a good plan. Eat well, drink plenty of water, and rest when the baby rests.
I will try, doctor. Thank you for your time.
My pleasure, madam. Go and enjoy that little one.

physical_examination.finding: womb has gone back to its normal size

clinical_actions.description: Start walking and pelvic floor exercises, build up to yoga slowly
Avoid very heavy lifting for a few more weeks
